entries.q: IBD lowered follow-through day threshold 1.7% to 1.2% ...
entries.claim: IBD originally: FTD = rise of at least 1% in one major average on volume above previous day; 'a few years ago' changed to 1.7% (volatility). Author (Rob Hanna, Jan 2008) describes the then rule as 1.7%+ up day on higher volume than previous day and higher than 50-day average volume, market not trading below the first rally day low in the interim.

Hanna cites HTMMIS 2002 edition p.65: O'Neil once used 1%, then 'we've moved the requirement up to 2%' because institutions manipulated a few Dow stocks to create false signals; 'originally 1%, now 1.7% (and for a while 2%)'; O'Neil never backed off 'no bull rally without a follow-through day'. Hanna's tests: 1.7% version missed ~20% of rallies; FTDs 'somewhat predictive', <=50% accurate without his tweaks.

entries.q: 'Follow-Through Day Tells You That It's Go Time To Buy Stocks'
entries.url: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/day-tells-time-buy-stocks-215900253.html (IBD article syndicated on Yahoo; date not retrieved)
entries.claim: FTD on Day 4 or later; best on Days 4-7; 'Generally, the gain should be at least 1% to 1.25%' (rough guide); 'Volume must rise vs. the prior session; it doesn't need to be above average'; Day 2 and 3 action irrelevant as long as index doesn't undercut its recent low; if it undercuts, rally attempt fails; don't immediately get fully invested; leading stocks break out and leave you behind if unprepared; use Nasdaq composite or S&P 500 rather than the Dow.

entries.q: aaii 'The Big Picture: How to Decipher What the Market Is Saying'
entries.claim: O'Neil (AAII): cluster of down days on heavier volume = distribution (institutional selling); 'usually takes three to five distribution days over a period of up to four weeks to turn the market's uptrend into a downtrend'; journal piece: 'three to five distribution days over a week or two can kill even the strongest bull market'; wait for a follow-through day; a few large institutions can run up the averages on one day to create the impression of a follow-through.

entries.q: 'How Do You Spot A Major Stock Market Top? Here's The Easy Way'
entries.claim: Distribution day = drop of 0.2% or more on the Nasdaq composite or S&P 500 in volume higher (on the Nasdaq and NYSE, respectively) than the prior session; market could probably withstand six or seven distribution days before rolling over; IBD research: don't count distribution days after 25 trading days; a 6% intraday rise from the close of the distribution day removes it; count published in Market Pulse with The Big Picture.

entries.q: 'Watch For Distribution Days...' / 'Looking For Next Market Top? Try Tracking Distribution Days'
entries.claim: Five or six clear distribution days over a few weeks before they pose problems; rule of thumb three to five on any one index within four to five weeks (one of these); 25-day expiry.
IBD video (Investor's Corner) summary: removed when an index rises 5% on an intraday basis from its close on the distribution day; forum: 25 days or index up 6%+; glossary inconsistent 5%/6%.

entries.url: https://discussion.fool.com/t/ibd-market-school/112218?page=7 ; https://www.tradingview.com/script/4iQbqb6k-IBD-Distribution-Tracker/ ; https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/distribution-days/ ; IBD title 'Stalling Signals An Early Warning For Stock Market' (inkl.com, unreachable)
entries.claim: Market School notes: stalling = heavy volume without further upside progress, usually at or near new highs; forum criteria 0%-0.4% gain, higher volume, close in lower half of range, count first stall day only; IBD-linked: index climbs but gives back most of its gain by the close / closes higher but in lower half of range; IBD does not publish exact thresholds; stalling applied less consistently than the 0.2% rule.

For years Market Pulse had three states (confirmed uptrend / uptrend under pressure / market in correction); in August 2024 IBD expanded to five exposure levels 0-20% ... 80-100%; IBD does not publish its formula; 'uptrend under pressure could mean nearly fully invested or mostly cash'. Third-party tweets: IBD moved to 'Market in Correction' suggesting 0% to 20% long exposure (posts dated ~2024-04 and ~2025-03 per search summary).

entries.q: 'How To Use IBD Market Pulse To Make Money With ETFs'
entries.claim: IBD ETF study (about a decade old): QQQ 100% in confirmed uptrend, 50% under pressure, 0% in correction; Market Pulse uses price and volume on Nasdaq and S&P 500.
Forum: five-level scale; 80-100% uptrend well in place; 60-80% gaining steam; 40-60% reset after downgrade from confirmed uptrend to under pressure; 20-40% after heavy distribution.

William O'Neil + Co. Market View: labels Confirmed Uptrend / Uptrend Under Pressure / Rally Attempt / Downtrend; rally attempt begins when a major index closes higher than previous day after a potential low (day one); 'A follow through day is a move of +1.7% or more on volume higher than the prior session'; upgrade to Confirmed Uptrend on FTD or on a close at a new all-time high; status shifts back to Downtrend should recent lows undercut.

Secondary: Day 1 can be a day that undercuts the low then closes in the upper half of its range ('pink' rally day); strict version: undercut then close above open. Failure = later undercut of the Day 1 low (sources vary intraday vs close).

O'Neil 1999 AAII sell rules: 'the general market averages have clearly topped and several of the market leaders showed climax top action'; ask whether the market is weak/acting poorly or in a normal decline; look for confirmation or divergence in the three major indexes. Yahoo piece: chapter nine of HTMMIS covers market direction; being right on all other factors doesn't help if the market heads down; 'three to six days over four to five weeks ... the general market will almost always turn down'.

entries.claim: Market School (Webster, Neilson/Nielsen, Harris): rules on FTD, 21-/50-day lines, distribution, Market Exposure, Buy Switch, Restraint Rule, Power Trend; forum-transcribed exposure ladder buy signal 1 -> 30% ... 5 -> 100%; circuit breaker -> exposure 0, Buy Switch off, Power Trend ends; power trend not a buy signal itself, time to be especially invested; exposure never increased on a down session.
AAII (CAN SLIM summary): stocks making the new high list with a big increase in volume may be prospects (stock-level N criterion). No O'Neil/IBD market-level new-highs-count rule found.
